references.text: Abraham offers water to wash the feet of his guests, illustrating the Old Testament custom of foot washing as a sign of hospitality.
Lot invites the angels in and offers to wash their feet, an example of the hospitality custom that Simon failed to show Jesus.
Joseph's servant gave water to wash the feet of Joseph's brothers, an example of common hospitality in ancient Israel.
The old man in Gibeah washed the feet of the Levite and his companions as a sign of hospitality—the same custom Simon neglected.
Abigail says she will wash the feet of David's servants, showing humility and service—a parallel to the woman's action toward Jesus.
The context of the verse: the sinful woman who wet Jesus' feet with her tears, dried them with her hair, kissed them, and anointed them with ointment.
Jesus continues his comparison between Simon's lack of hospitality and the woman's overflowing acts of love—kissing and anointing.
Jesus washes the disciples' feet himself, showing that foot washing was an important act of hospitality and a gesture of humble service.
Paul mentions the washing of the saints' feet as a mark of a godly widow, indicating that foot washing was an important service in the early church.
